purpose: Oxymorphone is used to treat moderate to severe pain that is not well controlled by other pain medicines. The extended-release form is used around the clock for ongoing pain. It is only used when other treatments are not enough to manage your pain.
how_it_works: Oxymorphone works by attaching to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord called opioid receptors. When it attaches to these receptors, it blocks pain signals from traveling through your body to your brain. This helps reduce the feeling of pain so you feel more comfortable.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, headache, dry mouth, and sweating are the most common side effects. Constipation is very common with this medicine, so drinking plenty of water and eating fiber can help.
warnings: This is a strong opioid and can cause slowed or stopped breathing, which can be life-threatening especially if taken in high doses. Do not drink alcohol or take other sedatives with this medicine as it greatly increases your risk of serious harm or death. It can be habit-forming and should only be taken exactly as prescribed. Never share this medicine with anyone else. Keep out of reach of children. If you or someone nearby stops breathing or cannot be woken up, call 911 immediately.
typical_dosing: For adults not used to opioids, the usual starting dose is 5 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain. The extended-release tablet is usually started at 5 mg every 12 hours. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how well your pain is controlled and how you tolerate the medicine. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
